Alvarez2006_10-5424-sjar-2006044-205.reason: Paired Class-A pans in Cartagena: one covered by black polyethylene shade cloth suspended 0.30 m above water (single or double layer), other uncovered reference; overall reduction factor fR = 1 - ES/EOP reported (0.751 and 0.835).
Alvarez2006_10-5424-sjar-2006044-205.notes: Shade screen 3 m wide on open light metal frame 0.30 m above water, fully shading the pan (phi = 1, computed from geometry; shade-cloth porosity/shade % not reported; solar transmissivity 6.4% single, 0.8% double). May-June 2003, 10-day runs per configuration. Evaporation by communicating vessel on electronic balance, hourly. fR includes condensation on/under the screen (fraction of evaporation reduction due to condensation 14.5% and 22.1%; abstract rounds to 14 and 21% of daily evaporation losses; condensation ~0.7 mm/day). Water area from standard Class-A pan dimensions (1.21 m diameter), not stated in paper. Wind under screen V15 = 0.086 V200 (1-BPE), 0.063 V200 + 0.02 (2-BPE). Daily E values not reported numerically (Fig. 5 shows hourly; open pan peak ~0.7 mm/h, shaded ~0.2 mm/h). Discussion also estimates reductions of ~79% (1-BPE) and ~86% (2-BPE) from the measured reductions of hv and delta-es (simple multiplicative estimate, not separate conditions). Economic analysis extrapolates fR to farm dams (context).

(2006). Chapters 4-7 concern evaporation formulas and models without covers.
JM2009_10-31428-10317-792.same_study_as: Martinez-Alvarez, Baille, Molina Martinez, Gonzalez-Real 2006, Agric. Water Manage. (efficiency of shading materials in reducing evaporation)
JM2009_10-31428-10317-792.notes: Estacion Experimental Agroalimentaria Tomas Ferro (UPCT, Cartagena). Two Class A evaporation pans (section 8.2.1, Fig. 8.1, book p. 166 / PDF p. 193): one shaded with the cloth, one reference. Cloth suspended 0.5 m above the pan (book p. 170) and shading the whole pan, so phi = 1 (shaded fraction), mode suspended. Under the cloths wind speed near the water fell by about 90% relative to 2 m wind vs about 40% without cloth (book p. 168). Experiment dates in 2003 (e.g. 14-5-03, 27-5-03); number of days per material not given on the rendered pages. Optical properties of the cloths in Tables 8.1-8.2. Thesis Table 8.3 gives 73.1% for single black PE vs 75.1% in the 2006 article (per first reviewer). Hourly curves (Fig. 8.8-8.9) show night condensation on dark cloths.
